newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka to use Telecom proceeds to retire debt.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka to use Telecom proceeds to retire debt.

text.p: The Sri Lankan government said on Tuesday it was using most of the money raised through the sale of a 35 percent stake in Sri Lanka Telecom to retire 10 billion rupees ($170 million) worth of treasury bills immediately.
Sri Lanka sold the stake and management in the telephone monopoly to Japan's Nippon Telephone and Telegraphic Corp (NTT) on Tuesday for $225 million.
A statement from the finance ministry said on Tuesday that the decision to immediately retire the debt would save the government 1.5 billion rupees in interest payments.
"The government considers the reduction of treasury bill limit as a durable step towards stabilising interest rates," it said.
Market analysts earlier said the government move to retire a portion of its treasury bill holding, now standing at about 125 billion rupees, could reduce pressure on interest rates.
Interest rates in Sri Lanka have fallen substantially since last year when the economy slowed, but the government wants to lower them further to boost investments.
Average commercial bank prime lending rates were at 13.4 percent in the week ending August 1 against 19.7 percent a year ago.
